title: Visual refresh for Standard Demo Deck v1 templates (typography, diagrams, screenshot style)
creator: Soojin Lee
project: Standard Demo v1 (Demo tenant + deck + talk track)
description:
Context
The Standard Demo Deck v1 is being used live with prospects. We need a light visual refresh so the deck looks consistent across presenters and regions, and so screenshots/diagrams remain legible when screen-sharing.

This is NOT a rebrand. Keep changes within Redwood’s existing brand constraints; goal is clarity + consistency + speed of updates.

Goals
1) Improve readability in screen-share: typography scale, contrast, spacing, and tighter hierarchy.
2) Create a consistent diagram style for: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, routing/fallback, observability workflow.
3) Publish screenshot style guidelines so Console screenshots are consistent (cropping, redaction, callouts, device scaling), and easy to keep updated.

Non-goals
- New logo/identity work.
- Re-illustrating the entire deck; only the recurring components.
- Any changes that require Console engineering work beyond minor label fixes already tracked elsewhere.

Deliverables
A) Google Slides template updates (Deck - Redwood Standard Demo)
- Updated title + section divider layout (clearer chaptering for choose-your-own-adventure branches).
- Updated body layouts (2-column, 3-up proof points, “problem → approach → proof” slide).
- Callout components: arrows, numbered steps, highlight boxes, “persona sidebar” box.
- Appendix layouts: security FAQ snippets, deployment options comparison.

B) Diagram kit (reusable components)
- Deployment modes diagram: Hosted / Dedicated / Private (consistent icons, consistent terminology).
- Smart routing + fallback: request → policy routing → primary model → fallback model/region (include failure path).
- Observability flow: request trace → token cost/latency breakdown → dashboards/alerts.
- Use a single visual system: consistent stroke weights, corner radius, and label style.

C) Console screenshot style guide (1–2 pages)
- Standard viewport: 1440px wide capture preferred; avoid browser zoom > 110%.
- Always show left nav + page title for orientation.
- Crop rules: keep context (breadcrumbs + key settings), remove empty whitespace.
- Redaction rules: blur API keys, email addresses, tenant identifiers; do not show customer names. Use generic “demo” identifiers only.
- “Demo-safe data” rules: prefer seeded data and known-good scenarios; do not screenshot live logs with unreviewed content.
- Callouts: use template callout components (no ad-hoc shapes); max 3 callouts per screenshot.
- Color/contrast: ensure charts are legible on typical video-call compression.
- Versioning: every screenshot asset must include a small footer note (Console build month or “Console 2025.02”) so we can audit drift later.

D) Typography + layout decisions (documented)
- Slide title scale, body scale, minimum font sizes for screen-share.
- Code style for curl snippets (monospace size + line wrapping rules).
- Spacing system (8pt grid guidance) for consistent layout.

Acceptance criteria
- Deck reviewers (PMM + SE + Sales) can apply the template to the working deck with minimal rework (< 60 minutes to migrate ~20 slides).
- At least 3 core diagrams swapped into the working deck without readability regressions during screen-share.
- Screenshot style guide is published and referenced by the deck working doc; screenshots in v1 deck conform to the guide.
- Provide a “how to update screenshots” checklist to reduce drift when Console UI changes.

References / linked assets
- Drive: Deck - Redwood Standard Demo (Working)
- Drive: Console Clickpath Screenshots - v1
- Confluence: Standard Demo Deck v1 (slide-by-slide intent)
- Notes: Dry run feedback flagged inconsistent typography + messy screenshot crops as recurring issues.

Open questions
- Do we standardize the deck background to light-only for contrast (recommended), or support dark variant? Current recommendation: light-only for this v1 due to screenshot consistency.
- Diagram icon source: use existing Redwood icon set if available; otherwise create minimal set (Hosted, Dedicated, Private, Shield/Security, Graph/Observability, Chip/GPU).
